newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - BT puts bought ahead of dividend payment.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - BT puts bought ahead of dividend payment.

text.p: Traded options in UK oil and telecommunications shares were busy as the underlying shares firmed on Monday, dealers said.

The purchase of slightly in-the-money puts in British Telecommunications may have been to lock in profits ahead of a special dividend of 35p net plus a final dividend of 11.95p by the company subject to completion of the merger with American telecommunications group MCI.
The deal was to buy 1,000 August 500 puts at 58p by an existing shareholder in BT. Once the stock has gone ex-dividend, the puts can be exercised to sell BT shares at 500p.
After collecting the dividend, the trader should be left with an overall profit.
By 1450 GMT, BT shares were up 11-1/2p to 469-1/2p.
Over in oil and gas explorer Lasmo the main deal was a short strangle established by selling 800 November 260 puts at 9p along with 800 November 300 calls at 13p.
The deal will make a maximum profit of 22p if the underlying shares are anywhere between 260p and 300p because both options will then be worthless. Lasmo shares were up 1-1/2p to 276-1/2p.
British Petroleum options were busy owing to profit-taking. The shares gained 1/2p to 752p.

Elsewhere, in FTSE 100 index options the main deals were volatility trades in which an options position was taken which was hedged by an opposite position in FTSE futures so that a change in market volatility will make the deal profitable.
One such deal was to buy 1,000 September 4525 calls at 258p in European style FTSE against selling June futures at 4680, which will make a profit if market volatility increases.
By 1450 GMT, cash FTSE was up 37.5 at 4682.5 while June futures were up 44 points at 4700.
